paper_metadata.title: A Quantum Online Portfolio Optimization Algorithm

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based quantum online portfolio optimization algorithm using quantum state preparation, amplitude-estimation-based inner product estimation, and quantum multi-sampling. It achieves a theoretical runtime Õ(T^3 √(n/r_min) log^{1.5}(1/δ)) compared with the best analyzed classical variant Õ(T^2 n log(T/δ)), yielding a quadratic speedup in the number of assets n while maintaining a regret bound of (12/r_min)√(log n /(2T)).

experiments.description: The paper’s main gate-based quantum experiment: an online portfolio optimization algorithm that replaces classical inner-product estimation, state preparation, and multi-sampling with quantum subroutines to update portfolio weights over T trading days.

algorithm.variant: Quantum online portfolio optimization algorithm (Algorithm 4) using quantum state preparation, quantum inner product estimation, and quantum multi-sampling

hyperparameters.delta: failure probability parameter; theorem stated for delta in (0,1/3)
hyperparameters.s: number of samples per day; chosen as in the sampling-based construction, scaling as O(T log(T/delta))

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum query access to price-relative vectors rho^(t) via oracles U_rho(t) acting as |j>|0> -> |j>|rho_j^(t)>; portfolio weights are represented implicitly through quantum state preparation rather than explicit classical storage
problem_formulation.objective_function: Online portfolio selection maximizing cumulative log wealth LS = (1/T) sum_t log(w^(t) · rho^(t)) with regret against the best fixed portfolio in hindsight
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No short-selling; portfolio weights are nonnegative and sum to 1; transaction cost modeled as fixed cost C per invested asset; approximate updates handled via erroneous exponentiated-gradient update with relative-error inner-product and normalization estimates

problem_instance.description: Online portfolio optimization over T discrete trading days and n assets, with adversarially revealed price-relative vectors

dataset_specification.description: Price relatives rho_i^(t) satisfy r_min <= rho_i^(t) <= 1 and max_i rho_i^(t)=1; no specific market dataset or ticker list is given

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Uses closing prices; assumes closing price at day t equals opening price at day t+1; converts to price relatives rho_i^(t)=R_i^(t)/R_max^(t)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical regret and runtime analysis; no numerical benchmark runs reported

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical arithmetic model assumed; no specific solver used
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct qRAM-like access to price-relative oracles; prepare sampling data structure and compute approximate inner products/norms
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure sampled assets and compute realized log-wealth / regret

speedup_claims.conditions: gate-based quantum algorithm with quantum state preparation, quantum inner product estimation, and quantum multi-sampling; asymptotic runtime stated as O~(T^3 * sqrt(n / r_min) * log^{1.5}(1/delta))
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper gives a theoretical asymptotic speedup only; no hardware experiment or benchmark implementation is reported. The quantum regret bound is worse by a constant factor than the classical baseline.

speedup_claims.conditions: comparing the n-dependence of runtime; Algorithm 1 runs in O(Tn) while Algorithm 4 is O~(T^3 sqrt(n/r_min) log^{1.5}(1/delta))
speedup_claims.caveats: The comparison is asymptotic and includes additional T and r_min dependence in the quantum algorithm.

speedup_claims.conditions: using quantum multi-sampling subroutine from Ref. [58]
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a subroutine-level claim, not an end-to-end experimental benchmark.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(T^2 n log(T/delta)) for the approximate sampling-based classical algorithm; O(T n) for the basic online update without sampling
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Worse by a constant factor in regret bound (12 vs 8 vs 2 in the paper’s theorem chain); runtime quadratic speedup in n relative to the classical approximate sampling-based algorithm

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not specified; asymptotic comparison only. Quantum runtime Õ(T^3 sqrt(n/r_min) log^{1.5}(1/δ)) vs classical Õ(T^2 n log(T/δ)).
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires oracle access to price relatives for all T time steps and assets plus arithmetic circuits implementing exponentiated-gradient updates; QRAM construction discussed in Section 4 would cost O(T n log n) time and O(T n) space.
limiting_factors: Only quadratic speedup in number of assets n
Algorithm requires large oracle access / QRAM for financial time-series data
Gate complexity scales as T^3 which can dominate runtime for long trading horizons
No resource estimates for fault-tolerant implementation

notes: No experimental hardware or benchmark implementation is reported; this is a purely theoretical gate-based quantum algorithm.

The paper explicitly states the use of quantum state preparation, inner product estimation, amplitude amplification, and quantum multi-sampling, but does not provide a concrete qubit count, depth, or gate counts.
The paper explicitly claims a quadratic runtime speedup in n relative to the classical approximate sampling-based algorithm.
However, the work provides only asymptotic analysis and no numerical or hardware experiments.
